generator: S9 aggregation step of the round-4 workflow (not a repository script), corrected by its batch-7 re-judgment step (correction, D50); every derived field follows the rules below
privacy: ids, SHAs, categorical judgments, counts and checked model-written paraphrases only: no login, mention handle, e-mail address, URL, repository name, model identifier or verbatim comment, PR or issue text

correction_record.use: the diffs of the 12 comments re-judged in batch 7 (s9_diffs_v2/) to the first later commit of the PR head that touches the commented file, that commit's S8a attribution, and batch_7.jsonl

judgments.record_unit: one batch and one judge: 6 batches x 2 judges, 25 comments each
judgments.canonical_form: json.dumps(records, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False), UTF-8, of the list as the workflow passed it (comment ids as strings)
judgments.superseded: the 24 judgments of the 12 comments re-judged in batch 7 (2 judges each) are superseded; they stay in each row's superseded key and no count uses them

judgments_batch_7.record_unit: one judge: batch 7, 2 judges, 12 comments each
judgments_batch_7.canonical_form: json.dumps(records, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False), UTF-8, of the list as the workflow passed it (records {judge, result: {judgments}}, comment ids as strings)

judges.kind: model agents; protocol §15.6 calls for two independent configuration-A agents. Their outputs reached this step from the workflow, for batch 7 as for batches 1 to 6, as judge 1 and judge 2; model identifiers stay in private run records
judges.inputs: batches 1 to 6 of the fetch record: per comment the pseudonymised comment text, diff hunk, PR title, linked issue title and body, and the pseudonymised diff of the commented file between original_commit_id and later_commit_sha (none where the commits could not be fetched). Batch 7 of the correction record, for the 12 comments whose diff was empty: the same text fields (2 model identifiers in one issue body masked) and the pseudonymised diff between original_commit_id and diff_commit, the first later commit of the PR head that touches the commented file (still empty for the one comment where no such commit exists)
judges.standing: model proposals, not human labels; queued for human coding

rules.judge_verdict: qualifies when the judge's request_type is behaviour_change or defect_report, its addressed is yes and its testable_offline is yes; fails otherwise
rules.qualifies: both judges' verdicts are qualifies; both commits were reachable in the S9 fetch: original_commit_id and the commit used (the sample's later_commit_sha, or diff_commit on a row re-judged in batch 7); and the commit used is agent-attributed under the S8a rule of scripts/screen_aidev.py (true by construction for the sample's later commit, which passed S8a; applied anew to each diff_commit)
failure_reason: commits_not_fetchable: a commit was not reachable because its repository could not be fetched; the comment fails S9 with this reason whatever the judgments
addressing_commit_not_agent_attributed: the commit used is not agent-attributed under the S8a rule; the comment fails S9 with this reason whatever the judgments (no row has it)
judges_disagree: one verdict is qualifies and the other fails; the comment is excluded and counted separately, not as a failure
otherwise both verdicts fail, and the reason is the first failed condition in the order of the protocol's criteria: not_behaviour_change_or_defect, not_addressed, not_testable_offline
rules.failed_conditions: every condition not met, in the order commits_reachable, commit_agent_attributed, request_type, addressed, testable_offline; a judged condition is not met when at least one judge says so (the rule is a conjunction over both judges), so for a disagreement it lists what the dissenting judge rejected; commit_agent_attributed does not apply where no later commit touches the file
rules.judges_agree: the two judges' verdicts are the same
rules.fetch_status: the repository's status in the fetch record: fetched, clone_failed or over_cap
rules.diff_status: ok: non-empty diff of the commented file between original_commit_id and the commit used (later_commit_sha; diff_commit on a row re-judged in batch 7); empty: the commit used does not change the file, which after the correction holds only for the row where no later commit of the PR head changes it; unavailable: not fetched
rules.diff_commit: only on the 12 rows re-judged in batch 7: the commit the batch-7 diff was computed against (correction record), the first later commit of the PR head that touches the commented file, found by walking the PR head's history from original_commit_id along the ancestry path; null when no later commit touches the file. diff_commit_agent_attributed: the S8a rule applied to that commit's AIDev pr_commits row (bot author account or agent co-author trailer); null when there is no commit. On every other row the commit used is the sample's later_commit_sha
rules.superseded: a row re-judged in batch 7 keeps its batch, diff commit, diff status, judgments and outcome from batches 1 to 6 under superseded, with the reason; every count, kappa, list and paraphrase uses the current values
rules.kappa: Cohen's kappa, (p_o - p_e) / (1 - p_e), with p_e from each judge's own marginals; request_type collapsed to behaviour_or_defect (behaviour_change, defect_report) versus other; addressed and testable_offline on their recorded categories; on the current judgments (batch 7 for the 12 re-judged comments)
rules.verification: for the 30 comments that at least one judge qualified in batches 1 to 6, both commits were confirmed as commit objects in the bare clones (git cat-file with every transport protocol disallowed, so nothing was fetched), the later commit's only parent is original_commit_id, and the diff file matches its sha256 in the fetch record. For the 12 rows re-judged in batch 7, with transports disallowed in the same way: original_commit_id and the PR head ref are commits in the bare clone; for the 11 with a diff_commit, it is a commit, a descendant of original_commit_id and an ancestor of the PR head, the first commit that git rev-list --ancestry-path lists for the commented path, every commit before it on the ancestry path leaves the file's blob as reviewed, its blob is the correction record's, and the diff file matches its sha256 and size in the correction record; for the other one, git rev-list lists no commit after original_commit_id on the PR head for the path, and the blob at the PR head equals the reviewed one
rules.s11_families: protocol §15.6, families and stopping: a family is one PR with a qualifying comment, and its earliest qualifying comment (AIDev created_at, then the lowest id) becomes the task's correction; at most 2 families come from one repository, its earliest PRs by creation time (AIDev pull_request created_at, then the lowest PR id). Applied here to the S9 survivors, before S10

paraphrase_policy.stored: only for qualifying comments: judge 1's requirement_paraphrase, after the checks below; null otherwise
checks: no login: whole-word, case-insensitive match against the logins of every participant of the sampled PRs (PR authors, review-comment authors on those PRs, linked-issue authors, commit authors and committers) and the repositories' owner names, read from the AIDev files in memory only
no mention handle and no e-mail address (the patterns of scripts/scan_tracked_files.py)
no URL and no domain name
no quoted text: no quotation marks or backticks, and no run of 6 or more consecutive words shared with the raw review comment, PR title, PR body, linked issue title or issue body
no pseudonymisation placeholder (role label or removed-address marker)
paraphrase_policy.result: 31 of 31 paraphrases passed; longest shared word run 5

s11_families.standing: provisional: computed on the S9 survivors before S10 has run. S10 can lower this count but not raise it; if S10 rejects a family in a repository with more than 2 qualifying PRs, that repository's next PR by creation time takes its place. The stop at 30 accepted tasks is not reached

agreement.population: all 150 comments judged by both judges, with the batch-7 judgments for the 12 re-judged comments, including the 19 whose commits could not be fetched (judged without a diff)

secondary.note: not requested by the protocol; reported for reading the main values

caveats.text: 12 comments had an empty diff in batches 1 to 6: the sample's later commit (the next commit of the PR's list) does not change the commented file, so the judges saw no change, whereas criterion 2 refers to the first later commit that touches the file. They were re-judged in batch 7 (correction, D50) on the diff to that commit, found by walking each PR head's history from the reviewed commit. 11 have one: at ancestry position 2 in 10 and 3 in 1 (behind a merge that leaves the file as reviewed); none is a merge, and each diff equals that commit's own change of the file. For 2180011139 no later commit of the PR head changes the file, so criterion 2 cannot hold on that head; it was judged again on the empty diff and fails on its request type. The earlier values of each row are kept under superseded. 3 of the 12 now qualify, and 2202777769, which had also failed only on addressed, still does (both judges: not addressed by that commit); before the correction 28 comments qualified, in 23 PRs and 12 repositories

19 comments in 4 repositories fail S9 because their commits could not be fetched: 17 in 3 repositories whose clone the session's GitHub proxy refused (HTTP 401), and 2 in 1 repository over the 300,000,000-byte cap. Both judges judged them without a diff; 3 of them fail on addressed only (unclear), besides the fetch.

under the S8a rule all 11 batch-7 diff commits are agent-attributed, each through a bot author and none through a co-author trailer, and each is in its PR's AIDev commit list after the reviewed commit. For 2258637033 the bot is the CI automation bot account (GitHub Actions), not a coding-agent account, and the commit is a linter's automatic fix rather than the agent's response to the review. It passes S8a as written, which counts any bot account; the comment fails S9 on its judgments (refactor_design, not addressed), so this changes no count here

the batch-7 text of 2477327497 replaces the 2 model identifiers of its issue body (in a code snippet) with a placeholder, so that no model identifier is written into any file; batch 6 keeps the original, and the correction record holds its sha256. The batch-7 judges saw the masked text; every other batch-7 text field equals its earlier batch

the judgments are model proposals, not human labels, and are queued for human coding (protocol §15.6). The S10 checks and the stop at 30 tasks are not applied here. The cap of 2 families per repository is applied only in summary.s11_families, to the S9 survivors before S10
